sentences.text: Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 19.10.2022 passed in MVC No.4795/2020 by the Court of the III Additional Judge and Member of MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (SCCH-18) (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10.11.2020 at about 5.10 a.m. the deceased Vijay Kumar, who was the owner cum driver of an Ertiga Car (Cab) bearing Reg.No.KA-51/C-8417, met with an accident while driving the Car on B.B.Road, Airport Road, near Bharathinagara Cross,
Bengaluru with a private Bus bearing Reg.No.NL-01/B- 1746, because of which, he died.
The accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Bus and at NC: 2023:KHC:29156 the time of accident, the Bus was duly insured with respondent No.1-Insurance Company.
The petitioners are the parents of the deceased, respondents no.3 and 4 are the wife and daughter of the deceased respectively.
The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.30,10,200/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Further, petitioners No.1 and 2 have been granted in total 20% of the compensation amount and respondent no.3 has been granted 55% and respondent no.4 has been granted 25% of the compensation amount.
It is further submitted that respondents No.3 and 4 had also preferred a separate claim petition which has been withdrawn.
4. Not satisfied by the award amount and the share apportioned in favour of them, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident happened on 10.11.2020 and the deceased was owner cum driver of the taxi involved in the accident and was a resident of Bengaluru.

As the income of the deceased was not established by the petitioners before the Tribunal, the same has been taken notionally at Rs.14,500/-
NC: 2023:KHC:29156 per month as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Company.
However, given the facts that the deceased was a owner cum driver of a taxi operating in Bengaluru, it can be reasonably assumed that he was earning about Rs.15,500/- per month.
Thus, under the peculiar facts and circumstances, this Court is of the opinion it is deemed appropriate to fix the income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.
6. The deceased was aged 33 years at the time of accident.

Thus, a multiplier of '16' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corp.

sentences.text: Taking the income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month, 40% has to be added to his income towards future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, the deceased,
who had four dependants at the time of his death 1/4th of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.31,24,800/- (Rs.15,500/-x12x16+40%x3/4).
NC: 2023:KHC:29156 7.

Thus, petitioners and respondents No.3 and 4 together are entitled to a sum of Rs.31,24,800/-
towards loss of dependency.
8. They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each towards 'loss of consortium', given the facts that the accident is of the year 2020.
Thus they are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,76,000/- under this head.
They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.
9. Thus, the petitioners and respondents No.3 and 4 are entitled a sum of Rs.33,33,800/- as against Rs.30,10,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioners and respondent No.3 and 4 are together entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,23,600/- (Rs.33,33,800/- Minus Rs.30,10,200/-).
Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.

10. In respect of apportionment of the compensation amount, the advocates for the petitioners and respondents No.3 and 4, after arguing the matter for sometime jointly submitted that NC:
2023:KHC:29156 petitioners may be granted 12.5% each of the compensation amount, respondent no.3 be granted 50% of the compensation amount and respondent no.4 be granted 25% of the compensation amount, with other conditions imposed by the Tribunal remaining intact.
Given the facts and circumstances of the case, I deem the same to be the appropriate.

Hence the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation awarded to the petitioners and respondents No.3 and 4 stands enhanced from Rs.30,10,200/- to Rs.33,33,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% pa. from the date of petition before the Tribunal, till deposit.
(iii) Respondent No.1-Insurance Company shall pay the compensation amount along with interest thereon within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

(iv) Each of the petitioners shall be entitled to 12.5% of the compensation amount along with accrued interest thereon.
